clue.text: Revise text starting at the end, identify high point

indicators.note: the word for revising text is read starting from its last letter, so it runs backwards

parts.note: to revise a text is to edit it
to mark something is to single it out or identify it

explanation.surface: An editor is told to work through a text backwards and pick out its climax.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the line left by water at its highest reach, so it marks a high point.

clue.text: Unsound artistic interpretation in play by Shakespeare

indicators.note: an interpretation gives the words a new reading, here a new order of their letters

parts.note: these two words supply exactly the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic complains of a shaky staging of one of the Bard's dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Andronicus is Shakespeare's early Roman revenge tragedy, his bloodiest work for the stage.

clue.text: Sketch plumage and head of swan with reductions

parts.note: to sketch is to draw
down is the soft fine plumage of birds

indicators.note: the head of the swan is its first letter

parts.note: the bird whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: An artist draws a swan's feathers while trimming the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawdown is a reduction, as of a reservoir's water level, troop numbers or funds.

clue.text: She may have said, "I like Ike" or, surprisingly, "I am me"

definitions.text: She may have said, "I like Ike"

indicators.note: the letters of I am me turn up unexpectedly in a different order

parts.note: the quoted boast supplies the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's campaign slogan is set against a self-absorbed boast.
explanation.walkthrough: I like Ike was Dwight Eisenhower's campaign slogan; his wife was Mamie.
explanation.definitionFit: Mamie Eisenhower, wife of President Dwight 'Ike' Eisenhower, would surely have endorsed his famous slogan.

clue.text: Dang! Headliner retreats

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the headliner's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the headliner of a show is its star

explanation.surface: A frustrated cry as the top-billed act pulls out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats is a mild exclamation of annoyance, much like Dang or darn.

clue.text: SS victory dividing French priests

indicators.note: the victory letter splits the French priests in two by sitting in the middle of them

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A military triumph seems to come between members of the French clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: SS looks like a steamship or the Nazi corps, but it is just two letter S's, each of which is a pair of bends.
explanation.definitionFit: Each letter S is shaped as a pair of bends, so two of them are a set of bends in a line.

clue.text: She used to escort you among texters, by the trees, in a storm

parts.note: people sending text messages write you as U

indicators.note: trees in a storm are tossed about, so their letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: these words supply the eight letters tossed about

explanation.surface: An old flame recalls walking someone through a tempest by the woods while everyone texted.
explanation.walkthrough: The you belongs to the wordplay; the definition is the woman who once led people to their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: An usherette was a woman who showed cinema and theatre patrons to their seats, a job now largely gone.

clue.text: Leap over part of a bank

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to jump over something using hands or a pole
second meaning: the secure strongroom where a bank keeps valuables

explanation.surface: A daring robber jumps over a section of the bank counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for springing over an obstacle and a noun for a bank's strongroom.

clue.text: Mistake that could make a shoe uncomfortable?

definitions.text: Mistake that could make a shoe uncomfortable?

parts.note: the real sense: an accidental wrong word said aloud

parts.words: that could make a shoe uncomfortable?
parts.note: the joke sense: a shoe's flap shifting out of place under the laces

explanation.walkthrough: A shoe has a tongue too, and if it slips out of place the shoe pinches; the phrase also names a verbal blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal slip is an inadvertent spoken error, saying something you did not mean to.

clue.text: Shocking, true version of Maria cut

parts.note: T stands for true, as in a true/false logic table

indicators.note: a new version of the words Maria cut rearranges their letters

parts.note: these two words supply the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes a disturbing, accurate account of a woman being injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something traumatic causes severe emotional shock, so it is shocking in the strong sense.

clue.text: Visiting Dot's frequent companion in Great Britain at the end of July

parts.note: in web addresses dot is often followed by com, as in dot-com
taken as written

indicators.note: the letter at the end of July is its last one

parts.note: the month whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A friend called Dot, often accompanied, pays a call in Britain in late July.
explanation.walkthrough: Dot reads as a woman's name, but it is the dot of a web address.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming by means dropping in at someone's place, paying a short visit.

clue.text: Sixty Minutes introduces one beautiful girl

indicators.note: the hour goes first and introduces, so leads in, the one that follows

parts.note: sixty minutes make one hour
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The TV news show 60 Minutes presents a profile of a lovely young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Sixty Minutes reads as the American TV news programme, but it is simply an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is one of the beautiful maidens of the Muslim paradise, hence any lovely young woman.

clue.text: Actor's tree-lined avenue Down Under

definitions.note: the clue's 's stands for is, so the definition is the actor himself

parts.note: Sydney is the biggest city of Australia, the land Down Under
a place lined with trees is green
an avenue is a street

explanation.surface: A performer's leafy boulevard is in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Sydney Greenstreet was the heavy-set British-born actor of The Maltese Falcon and Casablanca.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney Greenstreet was a film performer of the 1940s, famous as the villain Kasper Gutman.

clue.text: Furry mammal returns after a group of doctors drink

indicators.note: the mammal comes after the doctors, so it is placed second

parts.note: the AMA is the American Medical Association

indicators.note: the mammal comes back the other way, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: an otter is a furry river mammal

explanation.surface: An otter swims back to a gathering of physicians having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an Italian almond-flavoured liqueur, a sweet after-dinner drink.

clue.text: Agent covers the floor with snakes or lizards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is an agent
to tile is to cover a floor with tiles

explanation.surface: A sales agent lays a floor in a room full of creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes and lizards are both examples of the cold-blooded scaly animal class.

clue.text: Unbridled envy we erase with a night of revelry

indicators.note: freed from the bridle, the letters run loose and settle in a new order

parts.note: these three words supply all eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild jealousy is wiped out by a party night.
explanation.definitionFit: December 31 is traditionally celebrated with parties into the small hours, the classic festive night out.

clue.text: See 12
Primate discussed one type of theater

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken, so the primate's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the gorilla is the largest primate

explanation.surface: An ape is talked about in connection with a stage genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerrilla theater is political street performance staged suddenly in public places, a recognised form of drama.

clue.text: Euphoria about even just the first half of a promotion

indicators.note: the euphoria goes about, so surrounds, the half-word

parts.note: elation is great joy

parts.words: even just the first half of
parts.note: even has four letters, and just its first half is the opening two

explanation.surface: Even a partial step up brings great joy.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevation is a raising to a higher rank or office, which is what a promotion gives.

clue.text: Revolting creeps postpone fair

indicators.note: the creeps are in revolt, so their letters are overturned and rearranged

parts.note: the word whose six letters are rearranged
in American usage, to table a motion is to set it aside for later

explanation.surface: Rebellious lowlifes put off a carnival.
explanation.walkthrough: Table means postpone in the US; in Britain it means the opposite, to bring forward for discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A respectable result is decent but unremarkable, which is what fair means in a grading sense.

clue.text: See 15
We use the Roman variety in 25 or XXV

definitions.text: We use the Roman variety in 25 or XXV

parts.words: We use the Roman variety in 25
parts.note: the clue at 25 across is built from Roman number symbols
XXV is twenty-five written the Roman way, so the clue points at number symbols

explanation.walkthrough: The 25 reads as a plain number, written the Arabic way, beside its Roman twin XXV; it also points to the clue at 25 across, whose wordplay uses Roman symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Number symbols come in Arabic and Roman sets, and 25 and XXV show one of each.

clue.text: Shaker's associate: leader in music again

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
to do something over is to do it again

explanation.surface: A bandleader's partner on percussion plays the opening of the piece once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaker sounds like a maraca or the religious sect, but it is from movers and shakers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom movers and shakers pairs the two words for influential, powerful people.

clue.text: Energetic person's stimulating Monday

indicators.note: stimulating stirs things up, so the letters of Monday are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the day whose six letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A go-getter finds the start of the working week invigorating.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator, and figuratively a tirelessly active, forceful person.

clue.text: See 15
"It's cold outside!"—university vice president

indicators.note: the shiver word sits outside the university letter, enclosing it

parts.note: brr is the sound of someone shivering in the cold

explanation.surface: A shivering vice president at a university remarks on the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron Burr was Thomas Jefferson's first vice president, remembered for killing Alexander Hamilton in a duel.

clue.text: Three perfect squares are polite

wordplay.note: in Roman numerals C is 100, IV is 4 and IL is 49, the squares of 10, 2 and 7

explanation.surface: A mathematician remarks that three neat square numbers are well-mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the clue 20 across points to: the squares are Roman numerals. IL for 49 is not a standard form (XLIX is), but it reads as fifty less one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being civil means being courteous, behaving with good manners toward others.

clue.text: Misplaced equal sign is telling

indicators.note: the letters of equal sign are put in the wrong places, giving a new arrangement

parts.note: these two words supply the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An equals sign in the wrong spot in a formula gives the game away.
explanation.walkthrough: Telling looks like an adjective meaning revealing, but here it is the verb: informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeal is slang for informing on someone to the police, so squealing is telling on them.

clue.text: Outspoken knight nails extra duty

indicators.note: said out loud, the phrase sounds like the answer rather than being spelt as it

parts.note: a knight is called Sir, and to nail is to tack, giving Sir tacks

explanation.surface: A blunt knight hammers home an additional obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: Duty looks like a soldier's task, but here it is a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A surtax is an additional levy on top of a normal one, and a duty is a tax.

clue.text: Gym clothes screen organization or composure

indicators.note: here a verb: the gym letters dress, so surround, what follows

parts.note: PE, physical education, is the gym class at school

indicators.note: the letters of screen are organized into a new order

parts.note: the word whose six letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gym kit, a privacy screen, a company, or calm nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence, as in presence of mind, is calm self-possession, the steadiness that composure names.
